# pidginhost_public_ip (Resource)

A public IPv4 or IPv6 address allocated to the account, optionally attached to a cloud server. Every new resource allocates a new address.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pidginhost_public_ip" "web" {
  version          = 4
  server_id        = pidginhost_server.example.id
  reverse_dns      = "www.example.com"
  reboot_on_attach = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `version` (Number) IP version: 4 or 6. Changing it replaces the address.

### Optional

- `reboot_on_attach` (Boolean) Reboot the server when attaching the address, so its operating system picks the address up. Defaults to false.
- `reverse_dns` (String) Reverse DNS (PTR) name of the address. Attaching the address to a server sets it to the server hostname unless it is set here.
- `server_id` (String) ID of the server to attach the address to. Unset keeps the address unattached. Changing it moves the address in place. Terraform refuses to take the address off a server it did not attach it to.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) The IP address.
- `gateway` (String) Gateway of the address.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the object in the PidginHost API.
- `prefix` (Number) Prefix length of the address network.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a public IP by "<version>/<id>", since IPv4 and IPv6 addresses have separate IDs.
terraform import pidginhost_public_ip.web 4/12345
```
